yaml.title: Research
yaml.description: Publications and ongoing research by Haochen (Jerry) Li in deep learning, time-series forecasting, attention mechanisms, and quantitative finance.

markdown.markdown:
My research interests lie at the intersection of statistical learning,
deep learning, time-series forecasting, and quantitative finance.

My earlier work focused on computer vision and lightweight deep-learning
models. My current research studies attention mechanisms in nonlinear time
series and probabilistic forecasting for financial markets.


### Research on Lightweight Detection Algorithms for Unsafe Passenger Behavior on Escalators

Nan Zhang, Ying Hou, Qilun Li, **Haochen Li**, Wei Zhang, and Chaoyang Sun.

*2026 9th International Conference on Advanced Electronic Technology,
Computers and Software Engineering*, 2026.

This work studies lightweight deep-learning algorithms for detecting unsafe
passenger behaviour in escalator environments. It focuses on balancing
detection accuracy, computational efficiency, and deployment feasibility in
resource-constrained settings.

[IEEE Xplore](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/11504053/)

## Preprints

### Integrating Convexity and DeepLabv3+ for Semantic Segmentation of Power Lines

Ying Hou, Jindou Tuo, **Haochen Li**, Zhuoxin Yan, Xuemei Huang, and Yuqi Wang.

*Research Square Preprint*, 2026.

This paper proposes PLE-DeepLabv3+, a lightweight semantic-segmentation model
for detecting thin and low-contrast power lines in complex aerial imagery.
The model combines a reconfigured ConvNeXtV2 backbone, direction-selective
coordinate attention, efficient multi-scale feature fusion, adaptive edge
detection, and a class-aware focal loss.

[Preprint](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-8607246/v1) |
[DOI](https://doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.rs-8607246/v1)

## Manuscripts in Preparation

### When Does Softmax Attention Outperform Linear Prediction in Nonlinear Time Series?

**Haochen Li**

*Manuscript in preparation.*

This project studies the statistical conditions under which nonlinear
softmax attention can outperform classical linear prediction in nonlinear
autoregressive time series.

The central mechanism is a trade-off between the approximation advantage of
attention and its additional statistical estimation and search complexity.
The analysis develops signal-complexity thresholds characterizing when the
benefits of nonlinear attention become large enough to justify its greater
complexity.

The project also investigates approximate representability, projection gain,
multi-head attention, temporal dependence, and the empirical transition
between linear and attention-based prediction.

### Replication and Cross-Asset Extension of the Intraday Volume Estimator

**Haochen Li**

*Manuscript based on my UCL MSc dissertation, currently being prepared for
submission.*

This project replicates and extends a Transformer-based probabilistic
intraday volume estimator. The original framework is evaluated on U.S.
equities and subsequently extended to G10 foreign-exchange markets.

The model produces probabilistic forecasts through a Student-t predictive
distribution and incorporates asset embeddings, intraday temporal features,
and multi-step training. The study also investigates extensions from trading
volume to intraday volatility and market activity.

A central part of the project examines whether improvements in statistical
forecasting accuracy translate into economically meaningful execution
benefits. The empirical analysis compares ex-post and fully causal scheduling
procedures and evaluates their performance against historical intraday
volume curves.

A revised manuscript based on the dissertation is currently being developed
for submission.

## Current Research Directions

My current work focuses on the following questions:

- When does softmax attention outperform linear prediction in nonlinear time
  series?
- Which nonlinear structures and signal regimes justify the additional
  complexity of attention?
- How do multi-head attention and temporal encoding affect statistical
  efficiency?
- When do Transformer models outperform linear, tree-based, and recurrent
  baselines in financial forecasting?
- Can improvements in probabilistic volume and volatility forecasts produce
  economically meaningful gains in trading and execution?

## Research Areas

- Statistical learning theory
- Nonlinear time-series prediction
- Transformers and attention mechanisms
- Probabilistic forecasting
- Intraday volume and volatility
- Quantitative finance
- Computer vision and semantic segmentation
